# Rust API

ferx-core can be used as a Rust library for embedding population PK estimation in your own applications.

## Adding as a Dependency

```toml
[dependencies]
ferx-core = { path = "../ferx-core" }
```

## Quick Example

```rust
use ferx_core::api::{bind_covariate_stats, read_population_for};
use ferx_core::*;
use std::path::Path;

fn main() -> Result<(), String> {
    // Parse model and data
    let model_text = std::fs::read_to_string("model.ferx").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let mut parsed = parse_full_model_file(Path::new("model.ferx"))?;
    let (mut population, _) = read_population_for(
        &parsed.model, &parsed.covariate_decls, "data.csv", None, None, None, &parsed.column_map,
    )?;

    // Bind data-driven declarations (no-ops for a model without them)
    bind_theta_levels(&mut parsed, &model_text, &mut population)?;
    bind_covariate_stats(&mut parsed, &model_text, &population)?;

    // Run estimation from the model's own initial estimates and options
    let result = fit(&parsed.model, &population, &parsed.model.default_params, &parsed.fit_options)?;

    // Access results
    println!("OFV: {}", result.ofv);
    for (name, val) in result.theta_names.iter().zip(result.theta.iter()) {
        println!("  {} = {:.6}", name, val);
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

Why the bind step is there, and when it matters, is in
[Assembling the inputs yourself](fitting.qmd#assembling-the-inputs-yourself).
